rows.grounds: finite verb describing Māyā’s active initiation of worldly process
object of the action, the worldly round set in motion
instrumental indicating the means or regulating principle of the action
dative of purpose indicating the aim of maintaining the world

items.question: By what means and for what purpose does Māyā set the cycle of existence in motion?
premises: Māyā actively sets the cycle of existence in motion.
This activity proceeds according to established convention.
This activity also serves the purpose of protection.
items.inference: Māyā’s initiation of worldly existence is governed by convention and oriented toward protection.
uncertainties: samayā may also be read as 'by compact' or 'by appointed order'; 'by convention' is chosen as contextually fitting.
items.plain_english: She sets the cycle of existence in motion by convention and for its protection.
